Kids Kicking Cancer

By: Sinethemba Nogude | Paid

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We look at how one organisation is helping children overcome the rigours of cancer treatment through the art of karate.

Unique Selling Point:
Children Kicking Cancer
Cancer treatment can be debilitating , it takes a huge toll on patients both physically and mentally- especially if the said patients are children. This is a hard road to recovery.
With cancer comes a whole host of operations, chemotherapy ,radiation and medication , it can result in kids losing out on their childhood, but one organisation is trying to give children with debilitating chronic illnesses hope by teaching them Martial Arts . Kids Kicking Cancer is that organisation- supporting children through their rigorous treatments by coaching them in martial arts. 800-1000 children in South Africa are newly diagnosed with cancer each year, this is a trying time for the children as well as their families, and with resent COVID restrictions at hospitals... treatment can be lonely and filled with anxiety for children. With Weekly classes Kids Kicking Cancer teaches these kids valuable life lessons through the fundamental of the martial arts along with breathing and meditation techniques...These exercises are encouraged by Paediatric Oncologists , as these exercises and techniques can ease pain whilst the child is undergoing treatment.
This story is one of hope than anything else, these children are able to be children for the first time in a while , they are able to interact with other children going through the same ordeal and are most importantly able to enjoy themselves for the first time in a long time.
The sessions are mainly led by their “full of life” sensei Birgitt Smit, who is an amazing character and forms close bonds with the children. Though he has lost some of these kids to cancer she remains undeterred, and is determined to provide these kids with the space and freedom to live beyond their illness.
We will also have access to case studies at the Red Cross children’s hospital / Helen joseph who are undergoing treatment , and are part of Kids Kicking Cancer. I want this to be a human story, the story will be narrative based focusing on the children and their journeys through cancer treatment. We will document their journey.
I think this is a great human story of triumph of difficult odds and will resonate with our audience.

Further information:
Jake’s Story:

The first born the boeta the reliable the considerate the smart intelligent always running smiling. Ready for a race all of a sudden grew tired more days of the week than being up and happy...this is when we noticed the crack in his joy of being just a little boy after numerous clinic and doctors’ visits for a cough that is around more than it should be a loss in appetite a sore throat tiredness fevers visible lumps where every gland could possibly be I must admit that I became exhausted with the severity of my trips to the doctor that I made use of a chemist for over the counter quick fixes more often than I ever have my whole life...sure my kids had colds before but not one has ever been admitted to the hospital. We were not prepared for what came next
Excited little Jake got up on a Friday morning for an American day taking place at school me and his dad could both agree he woke up pale however he assured us he was feeling awesome and really needed to attend this event him and his peers were looking forward to since the announcement of it
But surly around 10am his class teacher contacted his dad his not feeling well we decided we are taking him to red cross children's hospital even though we did not have a referral letter from our local district lucky for us the nurse passing through saw exactly what we did the morning she pinched his finger and Asked for a folder
Turns out he didn't have any oxygen in his blood we had a blood transfusion were told he would stay for observation over 2 days we were then told he would have a bone marrow biopsy just to make sure his okay and that this problem would possibly be able to be prevented in the future
On the second morning of our stay my mother in-law had come to stay with him so that I could have a bath and see my other 2 kids and just breath unfortunately when I left the professor had been doing his round and explain he won't be able to give her the results upon my arrival back to my boy the nurses are collecting him to take him to another ward...I needed an explanation and was told it would be explained once we get there
It was around 11:30am on October 20, 2018
We got there and no explanation was needed there were some inpatients and some outpatients I dropped to my knees I was So uneducated about cancer and the abilities of its treatment and the success or failure rates thereof that not one positive thought came to my mind and that too was a drop in the ocean for the horror that came with treatment
I could not believe that my child and so many other kids are experiencing the excruciating pain that I was now witnessing. the first six weeks of treatment is crazy nothing is expecting the effects are domineering and erratic

Seth's story

So about our journey I'll try to make this a sweet and short as possible , Seth was diagnosed on the 7th May 2018 at Gatesville Medical Centre where he was then transferred to red cross hospital it was that night where life has changed almost forever I did not know what was ahead of me but I do know it changed my life in some good and bad ways. During the first few months of treatment I lost my job as I had to be at hospital almost every day and I was the only one who could be present as the rest of the family had jobs to fulfil and other daily living activities , Seth has under gone so much procedures, chemotherapy and lumbar punctures which became hard as he has to do a lumbar puncture without sedation and that is where Kids kicking cancer played the biggest role in breathing techniques , before he learned how to manage his breathing skills properly we struggled in procedure rooms on lumbar puncture days but as soon as he learned the breathing techniques from kids kicking cancer I saw a major difference as he now knows how to breath in and put properly whilst on that proceeding table which means soooo much to me as I was struggle to come with to terms with everything , if crying a river is true I could create an ocean of my own with only my tears there's soo much to add but I'll keep this short and simple I'm extremely overwhelmed as our 3 years are coming to an end in July 2021 where he'd ring the bell MD be in complete remission I can thank God for this and sparing us this far as so many kids lost their lives to cancer we are grateful to have come this far., so I'd like to tell all parents when your child is sick and complains about any pains or they are not feeling well in general please please please take them to a doctor to have them checked as Seth had the slightest of symptoms and never did I ever think it would be cancer and this is my advice to all parents today thank you.

The first thing that she asked, was am I gonna die. ‘No you are not going to die, we are going to kick cancer. We are going to go through this together…she undertood that im doing this and i’m going to win this battle.

UPSOUND FATHER:
I took him straight to the red cross because he didn’t want to eat. I bought him a gatsby because that’s something he loves. I told my wife that something is wrong with him and found out that he has leukemia. I was sitting there crying… I feel like I’m going to cry again. They gave him that thing that gives him a deep sleep and i told him hey, maybe you’re not going to wake up.

I know I have blood cancer… Leukemia and I was crying because it’s very painful - lumbar punctures and bone marrow and stuff like that.

So yeah, so they came, like a lot of tiredness, I was always tired. And you know,he has a younger brother was a few years younger than him and that little boy needed sometimes to strap Jake over his shoulder to take him just to take him to the toilet, even if it was for a vomit or if it was, for whatever if it was during this phase.
Visuals of Jake being handed his meds and taking them from his mom…
VO SIX: Three children with one thing in common, a devastating diagnosis that has completely changed their lives.

But with the help of one organisation- Kids Kicking Cancer these children found a way to fight through the excruciating cancer treatment
LINK: Power, peace, purpose - these are the three core values that “Kids Kicking Cancer” teaches children with terminal illnesses. Children often enter the program feeling anxious, scared and fragile but graduate feeling empowered and resilient.
VO SEVEN: Operating in several paediatric wards across the country Kids Kicking Cancer supports children through their treatment by coaching them in martial arts techniques. Martial Artist Birgitt Smit has been a sensei in the program for over 3 years
Claire; tell me about Kicking cancer… and what are the benefits for these children, to be here with you and to learn martial arts.
UPSOUND Birgitt:
These sick children, they teach us a lot about perseverance, about keep going … they’ve also got these little gloves … they are fighting these cancer cells and they do go through these ups and downs like you do with karate, but they are strong warriors that keep us motivated as well.
Claire: Practically what are they learning on their journey to recovery? OR What are some of the practical skills that they can apply to their journey when they are getting surgeries, taking medications, in their recovery?

UPSOUND BIRGITT Clips T765:
Okay, the main thing that we do with them is the softer part of karate, which is the breathing techniques. So I'm going to show you one just knife you up for it. And that is something that they can keep with them. When we are not around. If we go to the hospitals, we offer them some exercise, or we just break the routine that they in. So we offer them some sort of a skill to take away that is the breathing. So they can do that as at home as well. If they're feeling frustrated, or angry or sick, they can't sleep. So the breathing skill is actually the one thing we mainly focus on.

VO EIGHT: Every great martial arts SENSEI teaches that controlling your breathing is one of the fastest ways to reduce stress. And for children like Jake, Lerato and Seth, it’s a great way to take their minds off cancer and focus on just being… kids

Moses 15:30 :Many parents will say the first thing when we experience it no my child is sick until we explain to them It's not about the punching and kicking. It's really about the therapy, which is the breathing, the meditation and relaxation exercises. And we would invite them to come watch, because when you explain with words, sometimes good, don't get the message. So I'd invite them to sit. And now they are the ones who are now encouraging the kids come as could do your breathing.






Visuals of Moses teaching Karate to break up this this section…just a beat


Portia :14:27
She enjoyed the program. And because of the fear of needles, she really really had a fear of needles she's really really much better now
Chelsea 9:10 Jake finally got up and He didn't like to skip kicking cancer every day. Peyton : 14:00 They must breathe in ice creams, cakes, sweets and everything and exhale all the injections the bad things and it actually helped us so much. It really did help so much to incorporate.that was using those two he14:48 was actually using it especially in the lumbar punctures he was breathing in and he was breathing out and it helped us so much I will forever be grateful. Lead with Visuals of Jake and his mother interacting


V/O Head of Oncology at the RedCross children’s Hospital Professor Alan Davidson was amazed by the impact the program had on Paediatric Patients. Perhaps use visuals of Prof Davidson interacting with patients as a segway.

Upsound Professor Alan Davidson:It's rough. I mean, the cancer diagnosis in the first place will make you sick. And it is a truism that if you don't get treatment, you will get worse, not better. But unfortunately, that the treatment is is tough in order to cure the kids

UPSOUND Prof Davidson 02:56 :my eyes were opened when I watched Rabbi Ji do his first session here and kind of the whole methodology of, you know, helping kids to, to work through in little ways to work through those those pain barriers.
UPSOUNDTo actually put a number on it to say that the kids feel 10% Better or 20% Better is quite difficult. And that requires, it's going to require some interesting research. But I've no doubt that the children who have been involved in the program have felt better in themselves, and I would argue have been able to tolerate the treatment better.
v/o The road to recover fo Lerato,Seth and Jake hasn’t been easy, but through shear determination and bravery through the treatment and a little guidance from their senseis at KidsKickingCancer these little warriors have beaten the odds and have won the battle against cancer

We came all the way far away just to come have a conversation with you. And I think that people will be very proud of you.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): We look at how one organisation is helping children overcome the rigours of cancer treatment through the art of karate.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Children Kicking Cancer Cancer treatment can be debilitating , it takes a huge toll on patients both physically and mentally- especially if the said patients are children. This is a hard road to recovery. With cancer comes a whole host of operations, chemotherapy ,radiation and medication , it can result in kids losing out on their childhood, but one organisation is trying to give children with debilitating chronic illnesses hope by teaching them Martial Arts . Kids Kicking Cancer is that organisation- supporting children through their rigorous treatments by coaching them in martial arts. 800-1000 children in South Africa are newly diagnosed with cancer each year, this is a trying time for the children as well as their families, and with resent COVID restrictions at hospitals... treatment can be lonely and filled with anxiety for children. With Weekly classes Kids Kicking Cancer teaches these kids valuable life lessons through the fundamental of the martial arts along with breathing and meditation techniques...These exercises are encouraged by Paediatric Oncologists , as these exercises and techniques can ease pain whilst the child is undergoing treatment. This story is one of hope than anything else, these children are able to be children for the first time in a while , they are able to interact with other children going through the same ordeal and are most importantly able to enjoy themselves for the first time in a long time. The sessions are mainly led by their “full of life” sensei Birgitt Smit, who is an amazing character and forms close bonds with the children. Though he has lost some of these kids to cancer she remains undeterred, and is determined to provide these kids with the space and freedom to live beyond their illness. We will also have access to case studies at the Red Cross children’s hospital / Helen joseph who are undergoing treatment , and are part of Kids Kicking Cancer. I want this to be a human story, the story will be narrative based focusing on the children and their journeys through cancer treatment. We will document their journey. I think this is a great human story of triumph of difficult odds and will resonate with our audience.

metadata.Further information: Jake’s Story: The first born the boeta the reliable the considerate the smart intelligent always running smiling. Ready for a race all of a sudden grew tired more days of the week than being up and happy...this is when we noticed the crack in his joy of being just a little boy after numerous clinic and doctors’ visits for a cough that is around more than it should be a loss in appetite a sore throat tiredness fevers visible lumps where every gland could possibly be I must admit that I became exhausted with the severity of my trips to the doctor that I made use of a chemist for over the counter quick fixes more often than I ever have my whole life...sure my kids had colds before but not one has ever been admitted to the hospital. We were not prepared for what came next Excited little Jake got up on a Friday morning for an American day taking place at school me and his dad could both agree he woke up pale however he assured us he was feeling awesome and really needed to attend this event him and his peers were looking forward to since the announcement of it But surly around 10am his class teacher contacted his dad his not feeling well we decided we are taking him to red cross children's hospital even though we did not have a referral letter from our local district lucky for us the nurse passing through saw exactly what we did the morning she pinched his finger and Asked for a folder Turns out he didn't have any oxygen in his blood we had a blood transfusion were told he would stay for observation over 2 days we were then told he would have a bone marrow biopsy just to make sure his okay and that this problem would possibly be able to be prevented in the future On the second morning of our stay my mother in-law had come to stay with him so that I could have a bath and see my other 2 kids and just breath unfortunately when I left the professor had been doing his round and explain he won't be able to give her the results upon my arrival back to my boy the nurses are collecting him to take him to another ward...I needed an explanation and was told it would be explained once we get there It was around 11:30am on October 20, 2018 We got there and no explanation was needed there were some inpatients and some outpatients I dropped to my knees I was So uneducated about cancer and the abilities of its treatment and the success or failure rates thereof that not one positive thought came to my mind and that too was a drop in the ocean for the horror that came with treatment I could not believe that my child and so many other kids are experiencing the excruciating pain that I was now witnessing. the first six weeks of treatment is crazy nothing is expecting the effects are domineering and erratic Seth's story So about our journey I'll try to make this a sweet and short as possible , Seth was diagnosed on the 7th May 2018 at Gatesville Medical Centre where he was then transferred to red cross hospital it was that night where life has changed almost forever I did not know what was ahead of me but I do know it changed my life in some good and bad ways. During the first few months of treatment I lost my job as I had to be at hospital almost every day and I was the only one who could be present as the rest of the family had jobs to fulfil and other daily living activities , Seth has under gone so much procedures, chemotherapy and lumbar punctures which became hard as he has to do a lumbar puncture without sedation and that is where Kids kicking cancer played the biggest role in breathing techniques , before he learned how to manage his breathing skills properly we struggled in procedure rooms on lumbar puncture days but as soon as he learned the breathing techniques from kids kicking cancer I saw a major difference as he now knows how to breath in and put properly whilst on that proceeding table which means soooo much to me as I was struggle to come with to terms with everything , if crying a river is true I could create an ocean of my own with only my tears there's soo much to add but I'll keep this short and simple I'm extremely overwhelmed as our 3 years are coming to an end in July 2021 where he'd ring the bell MD be in complete remission I can thank God for this and sparing us this far as so many kids lost their lives to cancer we are grateful to have come this far., so I'd like to tell all parents when your child is sick and complains about any pains or they are not feeling well in general please please please take them to a doctor to have them checked as Seth had the slightest of symptoms and never did I ever think it would be cancer and this is my advice to all parents today thank you.
